correctness.rationale: The Fraïssé age has free amalgamation; every finite nonalgebraic one-point extension is exactly a link graph. A newly created forbidden tetrahedron occurs iff the three link edges on an existing tight triple are all selected. For paths/cycles the constrained pairs are respectively 2n-3 and 2n distinct consecutive/short-chord edges; each forbidden triple contributes the specified two-state matrix weight. Initial/final boundary vectors and the trace count all labelled assignments uniquely. The eigenvalue proof handles every n in scope; independent brute-force polynomial checks cover paths n=3..6 and cycles n=5..6, with an additional exhaustive n=7 cycle total.

value.rationale: The exact, edge-degree-refined finite-parameter nonalgebraic 1-type spectrum is a natural model-theoretic invariant. Tight paths and cycles are canonical overlapping hyperedge families, and the result proves a nontrivial two-state solvability boundary. The exact spectral decay base (3+sqrt(17))/8 exceeds the naive independent-constraint base 7/8; hence dependence has an exponentially measurable effect. This complete motivated infinite-family invariant is stronger than recomputing a finite table.
